name: simplex
title: Simplex Method for Linear Programming Problems

origin.description: Minimize or maximize the linear function a %*% x subject to A1 %*% x <= b1, A2 %*% x >= b2, A3 %*% x = b3, and x >= 0.
origin.usage: simplex(a, A1 = NULL, b1 = NULL, A2 = NULL, b2 = NULL, A3 = NULL, b3 = NULL, maxi = FALSE, n.iter = n + 2 * m, eps = 1e-10)

arguments.name: a
arguments.text: A vector of length n, the coefficients of the objective function.

arguments.name: A1
arguments.text: An m1 by n matrix of coefficients for the <= constraints. A vector is treated as one constraint.

arguments.name: b1
arguments.text: The right-hand side of the <= constraints, length m1. Required when A1 is given. Every entry must be non-negative.

arguments.name: A2
arguments.text: An m2 by n matrix of coefficients for the >= constraints. The bounds x >= 0 are already included and should not be repeated here.

arguments.name: b2
arguments.text: The right-hand side of the >= constraints, length m2. Required when A2 is given. Every entry must be non-negative.

arguments.name: A3
arguments.text: An m3 by n matrix of coefficients for the equality constraints.

arguments.name: b3
arguments.text: The right-hand side of the equality constraints, length m3. Required when A3 is given. Every entry must be non-negative.

arguments.name: maxi
arguments.text: FALSE minimizes. TRUE maximizes, by negating the objective coefficients and negating the optimal value on the way out.

arguments.name: n.iter
arguments.text: The iteration limit in each phase. The default is n + 2 * (m1 + m2 + m3).

arguments.name: eps
arguments.text: Tolerance for tests of equality. The default is 1e-10.

origin.details: The solver is the two-phase tableau simplex method. Each >= or equality row gets an artificial variable, and phase 1 minimizes the sum of those variables. A feasible point exists when that sum is 0. The artificial columns are then dropped and phase 2 optimizes the original objective from that point. With only <= constraints the origin is feasible, so phase 1 is skipped. The method is meant for small problems: the time grows about as the cube of the number of constraints. A bound x[i] >= b is cheaper to remove by shifting that variable before the call.
origin.value: A simplex object. soln is x at the optimum when the constraints are feasible. solved is 1 when an optimum was found, 0 when phase 2 hit the iteration limit, and -1 when no feasible solution was found. value is the objective at soln. slack and surplus are the final slack and surplus variables. basic holds the 1-based indices of the basic variables.
origin.example:
# This example is taken from Exercise 7.5 of Gill, Murray and Wright (1991).
enj <- c(200, 6000, 3000, -200)
fat <- c(800, 6000, 1000, 400)
vitx <- c(50, 3, 150, 100)
vity <- c(10, 10, 75, 100)
vitz <- c(150, 35, 75, 5)
simplex(a = enj, A1 = fat, b1 = 13800, A2 = rbind(vitx, vity, vitz),
        b2 = c(600, 300, 550), maxi = TRUE)

translation.usage: simplex(a, A1=None, b1=None, A2=None, b2=None, A3=None, b3=None, maxi=False, n_iter=None, eps=1e-10)

arguments.name: maxi
arguments.text: False minimizes. True maximizes, by negating the objective coefficients and negating the optimal value on the way out.

translation.value: A Simplex object. soln is x at the optimum when the constraints are feasible. solved is 1 when an optimum was found, 0 when phase 2 hit the iteration limit, and -1 when no feasible solution was found. value is the objective at soln. slack and surplus are the final slack and surplus variables. basic holds the 1-based indices of the basic variables. val_aux, a_aux, and artificial are set when phase 1 stops without a feasible point.
translation.example:
from boot.simplex import print_simplex, simplex

# This example is taken from Exercise 7.5 of Gill, Murray and Wright (1991).
enj = [200, 6000, 3000, -200]
fat = [800, 6000, 1000, 400]
vitx = [50, 3, 150, 100]
vity = [10, 10, 75, 100]
vitz = [150, 35, 75, 5]
print_simplex(
    simplex(
        a=enj,
        A1=fat,
        b1=13800,
        A2=[vitx, vity, vitz],
        b2=[600, 300, 550],
        maxi=True,
    )
)
